page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a constrained-core setup containing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 CPU architecture incorporates a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware instructions including AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory provides 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage includes a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD. It features no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates capable single-thread compute capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 31.35 GB/sec. Conversely, with only 4 vCPUs, multi-core throughput sits in lower tiers, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core result of 3990.17 and Clang compilation score of 5190.0. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth register at 37.14 GB/sec and 25.89 GB/sec respectively. LLM text generation on 7B models is slow at 4.5 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the constrained CPU core count paired with substantial RAM helps optimize per-core software licensing expenses without sacrificing working memory space. The fast local NVMe SSD delivers low-latency scratch storage directly on the host.
The server profile fits memory-intensive workloads that require moderate compute power, such as relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data analysis pipelines, and enterprise middleware.
